subject.title: fix(agents): enable tool-loop detection by default + add Anthropic spend-guardrail script

question: Should OpenClaw globally enable loop detection for existing unset configurations, and should an Anthropic/macOS/Slack gateway kill-switch be supported in core rather than as an external package?
rationale: Both changes establish durable product policy: one changes the default behavior of existing agent runs, and the other introduces a provider-specific operator control workflow with credential and service-management implications.

options.title: Keep the compatibility boundary
options.body: Retain the current opt-in loop-detection default and move the spend guardrail into an externally owned ClawHub-style package or owner repository.

options.title: Adopt a deliberate default change
options.body: Approve enabled-by-default loop detection only with documented upgrade behavior, compatibility coverage, and evidence that normal repeated-call workflows are not blocked.

options.title: Support the guardrail in core
options.body: Explicitly sponsor a core-owned operator workflow and define its platform support, credentials boundary, gateway ownership, and recovery contract.

recommendation.title: Keep the compatibility boundary
recommendation.body: Retain the current opt-in loop-detection default and move the spend guardrail into an externally owned ClawHub-style package or owner repository.

likelyOwner.reason: A current-main history pass is needed to route the default-behavior decision to the established agent-runtime owner.
